pr.title: Fix timezone handling in invoice due-date calculation
pr.body:
Due dates were computed in server-local time, so invoices near midnight UTC came out a day early for EU customers.

Closes #11

issue.title: Invoice due dates are off by one day for EU customers
issue.body: A customer in Berlin reports their invoice showing 2026-03-14 when it should be 2026-03-15. Looks like we're using naive datetimes.

files.patch:
@@ -1,9 +1,24 @@
-from datetime import datetime
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
 
-def due_date(invoice):
-    return datetime.now() + invoice.terms
+def due_date(invoice, tz="UTC"):
+    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).astimezone(ZoneInfo(tz))
+    return now + invoice.terms

@@ -1,2 +1,41 @@
-def test_due_date():
-    assert due_date(inv)
+def test_due_date_respects_tz():
+    assert due_date(inv, tz="Europe/Berlin").date().isoformat() == "2026-03-15"
